scene: Inferno IX — Furies, Medusa threat, protected sight and the opening of Dis
source: Dante, Inferno Canto IX: Furies upon the walls, threatened Medusa, heavenly messenger opens Dis
story: Virgil and Dante wait before the sealed city of Dis; Virgil's earlier attempt to gain admittance failed.
Three Furies appear atop the fiery walls and call for Medusa to petrify Dante.
Virgil turns Dante around and covers Dante's eyes with his own hands, protecting the living traveler from looking.
A powerful heavenly messenger arrives across the Styx, clears his way and rebukes the resisting guardians.
The messenger touches the gates of Dis with a wand and opens them without opposition.
Virgil and Dante enter the city and see open fiery tombs of the heretics; their individual encounters remain the next stage.

criticalDistinctions: A threat is not proof Medusa appeared or Dante saw her
Covering eyes preserves the possibility of later observation; it does not erase earlier observations
The messenger opens the gate, not Virgil alone
Dis remains shut until the messenger opens it
The three Furies are three characters, not newly assigned atomic positions
